articleTitle: Seismic constraints on Earth's small-scale structure
abstract: The small-scale structure of the Earth's interior is more difficult to access than the big picture. In the Bullerwell Lecture 2009, Sebastian Rost discusses seismic studies targeting small-scale structure at the core—mantle boundary, including areas containing partially molten mantle material and the remnants of subducted slabs, and assesses how they influence aspects of the Earth's dynamics.

articleTitle: Geophysical flows as dynamical systems: the influence of Hide's experiments
abstract: Michael Ghil, Peter L Read and Leonard A Smith recount the many and various ways that Raymond Hide has influenced their life and work in geophysical fluid dynamics, meteorology, climatology and planetary sciences, as well as in developing the study of dynamical systems in general.

articleTitle: Postgraduate degrees produce employable people — it's official
abstract: Academics in the field have long thought that postgraduate degrees in astronomy, astrophysics and planetary science and particle physics are a good bet for careers. But now a survey has confirmed that they bring excellent long-term employment prospects and above-average salaries, within sciences and elsewhere, boosting the case for funding studentships in order to support science and industry.

abstract: Digital cameras — inspired, of course, by astronomical research — are now ubiquitous. It seems that nothing happens anywhere in the world without it being recorded by a teenager and promptly uploaded to the net. This truism now extends to the edge of the atmosphere: a group of high-school students has recorded a video of the re-entry and disintegration of the Japanese spacecraft Hayabusa, from a plane over the Australian outback.

articleTitle: A place in space for the UK?
abstract: The Space Exploration Review, published in December 2009 and prepared as advice for Ministers concerning future UK involvement in space exploration, identifies potential costs and benefits of future UK space activity. Jeremy Curtis summarizes, on behalf of the review team.
Meeting report Nick Teanby and Neil Bowles look to the future for planetary geophysics, drawing together ideas discussed at an RAS Discussion Meeting in November.

Meeting report Massive stars make a profound impact on their surroundings, their galaxies and the evolution of the universe as a whole. Matt Austin and Dave Stock report on an RAS Discussion Meeting that considered current progress in understanding these complex stars.
